newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-J.White sees profit decline in 97/98.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-J.White sees profit decline in 97/98.

text.p: Malt manufacturer Joe White Maltings Ltd said its result for the year ending June 30, 1998 was likely to be below an expected record profit for 1996/97.
In a letter to shareholders, Joe White said it had already foreshadowed an increased profit for 1996/97 after reporting a net profit of A$6.81 million for 1995/96 in August.
"The result for the year ending June 30, 1998 depends mainly on barley purchases and malt contracts being negotiated now, for the malt year ending April 30, 1998," the company said.
Malt prices had been driven down in Europe, and the result would depend on the extent to which Australian barley sellers would share the burden of the damage to the export market.
"It is too early for a definitive estimate, but the end result is likely to be below the result for the year ending June 30 1997," the company said.
Joe White, the target of a hostile takeover bid by Ridley Corp Ltd, said it had not heard from Ridley since the failure of the bid was announced last week.
"We note their public statements that they will continue as holder of an 18 percent interest in the company," Joe White chairman S.E.K. Hulme said.
Hulme said he planned to meet with Ridley chairman John Keniry "when events have settled down".
